title: Depot Administrator
description:
Depot Administrator

Location: York
Contract: 6-Month Rolling Contract
Hours: 08:00 - 16:00 Mon - Thu ( 32 hrs a week )
Pay Rate: 13.87 per hour PAYE

About the Role

We are looking for an organised and proactive Depot Administrator to join our team based at our York depot. This is a varied administrative position that combines office administration and reception duties, providing essential support to the depot and helping ensure the smooth day-to-day running of the site.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced administrator who enjoys working in a busy environment and is comfortable managing multiple tasks while maintaining attention to detail.

Key Responsibilities
Administration
- Data entry and maintenance of company records and databases.
- Filing and document management.
- Producing reports and updating spreadsheets.
- Recording annual leave, overtime and Euroleave information.
- Booking employee training courses and maintaining training records.
- Raising purchase orders and processing expenses.
- Supporting the ordering and tracking of PPE, tools and other depot supplies.
- General administrative support to the depot management team.

Reception & Front of House
- Answering and directing incoming telephone calls.
- Managing shared email inboxes and responding to enquiries.
- Greeting visitors and ensuring appropriate site sign-in procedures are followed.
- Logging incoming and outgoing post.
- Arranging taxis and travel requirements when needed.
- Booking meeting rooms and coordinating meeting arrangements.
- Ordering stationery and maintaining office supplies.

Skills & Experience
Essential
- Previous experience in an administrative and/or receptionist role.
- Strong organisational skills with excellent attention to detail.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, Word and Outlook.
- Confident communication skills, both written and verbal.
- Ability to prioritise workload and manage multiple tasks effectively.
- Reliable, professional and customer-focused approach.

Desirable
- Experience raising purchase orders and processing expenses.
- Experience maintaining staff records, training records or leave trackers.
- Experience working within an operational, depot or logistics environment.

Additional Information
- This is a site-based role, working four days per week from the York depot.
- Standard compliance checks will apply.
- Training will be provided for specific processes, including overtime and Euroleave recording.
- Flexibility to work additional hours when required would be advantageous.

What We're Looking For

The successful candidate will be a friendly, approachable and highly organised administrator who enjoys supporting a busy team. You'll take pride in delivering excellent administrative support, maintaining accurate records and ensuring visitors and colleagues receive a professional service at all times.

Adecco is a disability confident employer. We are committed to providing an inclusive and accessible recruitment process. If you require reasonable adjustments at any stage, please let us know so we can support you.

We use generative AI tools to support our screening process to ensure a fair and consistent experience for all applicants. All final hiring decisions are made by our recruitment team.

If you do not hear from us within five working days, your application may not have progressed on this occasion. We encourage you to apply for future opportunities.

Adecco acts as an employment agency for permanent recruitment and an employment business for the supply of temporary workers. The Adecco Group UK & Ireland is an Equal Opportunities Employer.

description:
Training and Recruitment Coordinator

Location: Harrogate
Salary: Up to 33,000
Benefits: Company car, 27 days holiday + bank holidays, pension, life assurance and employee benefits
Hours: Full-time, with flexible start/finish times

The Role

Ashley Kate are pleased to be supporting our client in the search for a Training and Recruitment Coordinator based in Harrogate.
This is a varied role responsible for coordinating recruitment, onboarding and training activity across a large operational workforce. You will work closely with the Training Manager and hiring managers across multiple locations, with travel required approximately 2-3 days per week.

Key Responsibilities
- Coordinate the end-to-end recruitment process for operational and technical vacancies.
- Arrange interviews and liaise with candidates and hiring managers throughout the recruitment process.
- Coordinate new starter onboarding and inductions.
- Support pre-employment processes, including drug and alcohol testing.
- Work closely with operational and engineering managers on recruitment requirements and interviews.
- Maintain accurate recruitment records and documentation.
- Support the implementation and continuous improvement of recruitment systems and processes.
- Provide general recruitment and training coordination and administration.

About You
- Previous recruitment, recruitment coordination or similar experience.
- Experience within a high-volume or operational recruitment environment would be advantageous.
- Excellent organisation and attention to detail.
- Strong communication and relationship-building skills.
- Ability to manage multiple vacancies and priorities effectively.
- Confident working independently and taking ownership of recruitment activity.
- Comfortable travelling regularly between regional sites.
- Experience recruiting within transport, logistics, engineering, care or another high-volume environment would be beneficial.

Benefits
- Salary up to 33,000.
- Company car - electric vehicle.
- 27 days annual leave plus bank holidays.
- Pension scheme.
- Life assurance at 2x salary.
- Employee discount benefits.
- Flexible working hours.

title: Receptionist Part Time
description:
Are you an organised, approachable, and customer-focused Administrator looking to make a real difference in a Scarborough? Would you like to work for an organisation known for delivering high-quality client support and trusted by the community it serves? Are you looking for a supportive, client-focused organisation where teamwork and service excellence are at the core?

If so then this part time Administrator job could be right for you. This is a part-time, permanent role, offering variety in your day-to-day duties and the opportunity to provide excellent service to clients across the business.

What the Administrator job involves

As an Administrator, you will be the first point of contact for clients, ensuring they receive a friendly, efficient, and professional service. Your responsibilities will include:
- Handling client enquiries with care, offering guidance and directing them to the right services both over the phone and via email.
- Managing and booking appointments efficiently using the inhouse CRM system.
- Processing and distributing correspondence, both electronically and by mail.
- Supporting the wider team with administrative duties including data entry, filing, scanning, and record maintenance.
- Providing accurate information to clients and colleagues to ensure smooth communication across departments.
- Answering the telephone and taking accurate messages to send to colleagues at all levels within the organisation.
- Supporting the reception team by contributing to a welcoming and professional environment, in person and over the phone.

Skills required
- Experience of working within administration / coordination based roles previously or an office based customer service position.
- Strong IT and data entry skills with knowledge of Microsoft Office packages.
- Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal with the attention to detail to match
- A flexible, conscientious, and team-oriented approach.
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to prioritise tasks effectively.
- Pro-active and willing to learn a complex and new role

- Part time 18.75 hours a week

title: Office Administrator
description:
Are you a proactive and confident Office Administrator who enjoys working in a busy, sociable environment where no two days are quite the same?

Would you like to join a growing financial services business in Pickering, where you ll be trusted to manage your own workload, build relationships with clients and develop your knowledge along the way?

We are looking for an organised and personable Office Administrator to join our client s friendly, open-plan office.

This is a permanent opportunity offering plenty of variety. You ll be working with different systems, communicating regularly with clients and supporting the team with the administration needed to keep client records accurate, compliant and up to date.

You don t need to know everything about the industry day one. What s important is that you re proactive, confident communicating with people and comfortable taking ownership of your work. You ll receive training and development to build your understanding of the legislation and compliance and reporting as your job evolves.

The office is busy, chatty and collaborative, with a relaxed dress code and it s dog friendly too!

What the Office Administrator job involves

You ll provide day-to-day administrative support to the team while helping to ensure clients receive an efficient and professional service.
- Completing and processing client forms and documentation.
- Contacting clients to chase outstanding information, documents and signatures.
- Ensuring the required documentation is received and recorded for compliance purposes.
- Keeping client information and records accurate and up to date.
- Using a number of different systems to manage information and administrative processes.
- Creating reports and letters from templates to send to clients.
- Communicating confidently with clients by telephone and email.

This role would suit someone who enjoys taking responsibility for their work rather than waiting to be given their next task.

Skills required

We re looking for someone who is organised, approachable and comfortable working in a busy environment. You ll ideally have:
- Previous administration experience is essential.
- Strong organisational skills and excellent attention to detail.
- A proactive approach and the confidence to use your own initiative.
- Good written and verbal communication skills.
- Confidence speaking with people over the phone.
- The ability to self-manage and prioritise a varied workload.
- Good IT skills and the ability to learn and work across several different systems.
- A professional approach when handling confidential information.

Other information
- Full time working 8:30am 5:00pm Monday to Thursday and 8:30am 1:30pm Friday
- 20 days annual leave plus bank holidays.
- Your birthday off.
- Lunch provided each day.
- Access to free financial advice.
- Performance-related end-of-year bonus.
- Training and development including paid for professional qualifications.
- A friendly, open-plan and dog-friendly working environment.

title: Administrator
company: Tees Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
advertiser_name: Tees Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
description: We are looking to recruit a part-time, experienced administrator to join our friendly front of-house team based at Eastfield Clinic, Scarborough. Eastfield Clinic is an Adult Learning Disabilities base providing care, support, and information to people in the local community, there is free car parking available to staff. As an essential part of the reception team, you will be the first point of contact for Service Users, Carers, Staff and External Partners Whilst having previous experience in a customer service role is essential, NHS or other health care experience is desirable. We are first and foremost looking for a colleague with a passion for helping people who believes in delivering excellent customer service, who has a keen interest in learning and working in a health care setting with a 'can do' attitude. The post is 18 hours per week and will support the Adult Learning Disabilities at Eastfield Clinic. You must have the Right to Work in the UK in order to be successfully appointed to this role. Please note, this role does not meet the required eligibility criteria for sponsorship under the Skilled Worker visa and therefore the Trust is unable to offer sponsorship for this particular role. The main duties will require you to greet service users, carers, and external partners face to face including answering queries via telephone. The role will involve dealing with incoming and outgoing post, room bookings, order stationery, logging calls with estates, dealing with prescriptions, petty cash, booking taxis or patient transport, arranging collection of pathology samples, and general office duties. The ability to remain calm, communicate clearly, adhere to confidentiality, and promote a positive culture for those living with mental health issues and/or learning disabilities. The successful candidate will be expected to perform basic admin tasks, update clinic lists, maintain visitor logs, issue access cards, deal with incoming and outgoing post, support accurate data inputting onto the Trust patient database and ensuring that all information in the reception area for staff and the public is clearly displayed and updated as appropriate. For more details, please read carefully the job description. To be successful at shortlisting please briefly describe how you match this description citing examples to reinforce your experience. Please note we are unable to shortlist those who do not match the essential criteria. Our Trust is dedicated to supporting our colleagues in providing an excellent working environment and encourages everyone to share their progressive ideas. All staff have regular 1-2-1 supervisions and an annual appraisal, which provides lots of opportunity for celebration of achievements, and discussions around challenges, and your aspirations. You will work with established reception staff and be supported by the wider admin team. If successful you will be supplied with a job plan and a fully supported induction. For an informal discussion or to arrange a visit to Eastfield Clinic, please call: 01723 580 940 This is a rewarding role working in a desirable team, if you feel this is the challenge for you then we very much look forward to receiving your application. Please refer to the attached job description and person specification for further detailed information to ensure that you meet the role criteria before applying. This job advert may close early if a high volume of applications have been received. If interested, please apply for this post as soon as possible.

title: Team Administrator

advertiser_name: Tees Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
description: A unique and exciting fixed term opportunity (18 months) has arisen for an organised, conscientious and dynamic administrator to join our recently established Community Mental Health 'Hub' team. The Hub is a drop-in centre, located in the City of York Council building, at 30 Clarence Street in York. It forms part of York Mental Health Partnership's vision of support for adults across the city and will help change the way people are able to access mental health services. It is expected that the post holder will, as required by the service, work 'in the field' on occasion i.e. at the CYC building or events nearby. These locations and facilities will be easily accessible by car, bus and bicycle. As a member of this small and friendly multi-disciplinary team, you will work in both an office environment and alongside the team in the community. If you are looking for a new challenge, an opportunity to be part of a team striving to make a difference, enjoy variety in your work and have skills in project and process development, we will welcome your application for this role. You must have the Right to Work in the UK in order to be successfully appointed to this role. Please note, this role does not meet the required eligibility criteria for sponsorship under the Skilled Worker visa and therefore the Trust is unable to offer sponsorship for this particular role. Having significant previous experience as an administrator is essential to this role. NHS or other health/social care experience is desirable. We are looking for an individual with a passion for people, demonstrable customer service experience, extensive organisational skills, an interest in working in a mental health care setting and a 'can do' attitude. This role will be the heart of a dedicated and caring team and is a pivotal role in the day-to-day operations. You will provide essential day-to-day administrative support to the clinical team, ensuring that the processes you develop and put in place are sustainable and meet the needs of the service. This will enable them to provide the best possible care for the service users. We are looking for someone who feels comfortable in a public healthcare setting, can multi-task in a busy environment, can communicate confidently, is thorough and takes pride in their work, can build strong working relationships with a variety of people, can prioritise their workload and work to deadlines. With a starting salary of £25,760 per annum, a generous NHS pension scheme, a fantastic annual leave package (27 days annual leave plus 8 bank holidays) and access to other NHS staff benefits and discounts, it is fair to say that this job has a lot to offer. And, its not just the NHS pay scale and benefits that we offer that make joining our organisation an excellent choice, there are many training and development opportunities available, giving you the opportunity for career progression. All staff have regular 1-2-1s, quarterly supervision meetings and an annual appraisal, which provides lots of opportunity for discussion around achievements, challenges and aspirations. Staff recognition is very important to us; we work closely with colleagues to support development, the staff voice, and to recognise teams and individuals through our Greatix and Star Award schemes; highlighting the outstanding work being done every day. We recognise that Administrators are professionals and are a valuable asset to our organisation. We understand that they have a key role in the support and delivery of our services and that their contribution helps us in achieving our aim of consistently providing safe and high-quality care for our service users. The kind of care we would want for ourselves and for our loved ones. title: Part-time Receptionist
description: We are a small GP Practice with a very high level of satisfaction among our patients thanks to the dedication and professionalism of all our staff. As a Receptionist you are the first point of entry into the practice and therefore key in maintaining our reputation and our standards, whether in person or on the phone. In this role you will be faced by varied and sometimes challenging tasks, occasionally having to deal with some uncomfortable situations. Your communication and listening skills will be critical for this. This is an exiting and satisfying role as part of a small but happy and committed team. Main duties include greeting and assisting everyone who contacts the practice whether in person or on the phone, making, cancelling and rescheduling appointments with the clinical staff. You are expected to work 10-15 hours per week at different times respecting the agreed rotas. You are flexible and are able to do additional hours on other days to cover holidays and sickness of your colleagues. No weekend work is involved. In addition to permanent patient contact to assist them and deal with their queries you will also have additional administrative tasks to fulfil such as patient registration, information updating, scanning documents , calling patients based on requests from the clinical staff for specific requirements, etc. Depending on your shift you will be required to open or close the practice and perform the daily checks and controls associated with those moments. Good communication and problem solving skills and ability to multitask are key requirements for this position Please DO NOT USE AI to complete your application. AI generated replies WILL NOT BE CONSIDERED This position is offered as a temporary contract. This is an on-site position. Working from home is not possible. ------------------------------------------------------------------ Job responsibilities: To deal politely and efficiently with patients as the first point of contact for anyone visiting or calling the surgery. Dealing with patients and visitors professionally, efficiently, with empathy and courtesy. To ensure patient confidentiality is respected at all times and to adhere to the Data Protection Act. Make routine and emergency appointments for patient to see the doctors and nurses. Check patient details on clinical system. Deal with requests for home visits. Answer queries with regard to results of recent tests e.g. bloods, urine or x-ray. This includes contacting the hospital(s) for these results if necessary. Inform patients, when directed by a doctor, of the need to make a follow-up appointment at the surgery. Accurate completion of registration forms ensuring the existing patient information is correct and up to date andupdating it based on patients requests. Accept requests for repeat prescriptions, hand out completed prescriptions, cancel appointments when necessary, contact the patients (s) and re-book if required. Book patient hospital transport when required. Contact the emergency services when necessary. Filing, scanning and organising medical notes. Assist in ordering and stock control of relevant stationery. Check and tidy consulting rooms between surgeries and keeping waiting area clean and in order. In the morning, open the surgery and ensure everything is ready for the upcoming session. In the afternoon, close the surgery and ensure everything is locked up properly and the alarm is set. Administrative Duties Scanning documents onto clinical system.Other administrative duties as required and agreed. Ensure that reception area is tidy and maintain cleanliness in the kitchen facilities when necessary. Be flexible in being available for overtime in order to cover for colleagues' leave and sickness. Ensure you read all the Practice mandatory policies and that you complete all the mandatory courses. Any other relevant duties as mutually agreed.
